Validation and reproduction of published results

Source: vignettes/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd
library(DesignComplexSurvival)

The results of the package are checked in three ways:

  • the unit tests (tests/testthat/) compare the results with an independent Python implementation (inst/validation/python/, using matrix exponentials and adaptive quadrature) and, when the packages are installed, with gsDesign, gsDesign2, rpact and lrstat;
  • the scripts in inst/reproduce/ recompute sample sizes, numbers of events, analysis times, bounds, powers, expected study durations and conditional powers printed in articles and a statistical analysis plan;
  • the scripts in inst/validation/ compare the package with patient-level simulations, with the package PWEALL and with the decisions of lrstat::fseqbon(), and the expected values when the trial stops at the bounds and the conditional power with rpact, lrstat and gsDesign and with the examples printed in the vignettes of rpact and gsDesign.

The last two folders are run by their run_all.R, which judges every value as PASS (the criterion is met), EXPLAINED (the criterion is met after a registered explanation, such as an apparent misprint), FAIL, or INFO (not judged: a published value computed by a method that the package does not reproduce, or an asymptotic approximation compared with simulation). The results are installed with the package, and this article reads them:

judgements <- c("PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL", "INFO")
read_results <- function(folder) {
  utils::read.csv(system.file(folder, "results", "summary.csv",
                              package = "DesignComplexSurvival"))
}
rp <- read_results("reproduce")
vd <- read_results("validation")
count <- function(x, by) {
  tab <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(x[[by]], factor(x$judgement, levels = judgements)))
  tab$Total <- rowSums(tab)
  tab
}

Reproduction of published results

The scripts recompute 780 printed values from 18 sources. Each value has a criterion that reflects the rounding of the printed value, for example rounding up for a sample size or agreement to the printed digits for a power.

knitr::kable(count(rp, "source"))
PASS EXPLAINED FAIL INFO Total
Barthel2006 44 1 0 0 45
Erdmann2025 8 0 0 33 41
Glimm2010 20 3 0 0 23
KimTsiatis1990 223 12 0 12 247
Lakatos1988 2 0 0 16 18
Lakatos2002 0 0 0 16 16
Lu2021 19 1 0 24 44
Luo2019 29 15 0 4 48
MaurerBretz2013 11 4 0 0 15
OrtegaVilla2025 5 0 0 1 6
Porcher2002 30 5 0 24 59
Shih1995 11 5 0 4 20
Sugimoto2017 3 18 0 9 30
Tamhane2010 68 10 0 0 78
Tang2022 0 16 0 0 16
TorresSaavedra2026 3 0 0 0 3
Vergote2024 9 1 0 6 16
Xia2016 0 0 0 55 55

In total 485 values pass, 91 are explained, 0 fail and 204 are not judged. The sources, criteria and registered explanations are listed in the README.md and explained.csv of inst/reproduce/.

The expected study durations, numbers of failures and patients and the probabilities of stopping of Kim and Tsiatis (1990) are computed with the conventions of the article (for both hypotheses the analysis times found under the null hypothesis, and the correlations of the statistics from the information times) from the bounds, means, analysis times and expected events of the package; the expected values of ms_power(), which use under each hypothesis its own analysis times and the correlations of the information, are given next to them as INFO rows. The conditional powers of Ortega-Villa et al. (2025) are those of ms_cond_power().

Comparison with simulations and other software 

labels <- c(fastsurvival = "FastSurvival simulation",
            python = "Python simulation",
            python_two = "Python simulation, PFS and OS together",
            python_calendar = "Python simulation, switching from a calendar time",
            danzer = "Estimator of Danzer et al. (2025)",
            pweall = "PWEALL",
            lrstat_fseqbon = "lrstat::fseqbon()",
            rpact = "rpact::getPowerSurvival(), expected values",
            rpact_vignette = "Values printed in the rpact vignette",
            lrstat_expected = "lrstat::lrpower(), expected values",
            gsdesign_expected = "gsDesign::gsProbability(), expected values",
            python_expected = "Python simulation, expected values",
            gsdesign_cp = "gsDesign::gsCP(), conditional power",
            gsdesign_vignette = "Values printed in the gsDesign vignette")
tab <- count(vd, "source")
n_scen <- tapply(vd$scenario, vd$source, function(x) length(unique(x)))
tab <- cbind(Route = ifelse(is.na(labels[rownames(tab)]), rownames(tab),
                            labels[rownames(tab)]),
             Scenarios = as.vector(n_scen[rownames(tab)]), tab)
names(tab)[names(tab) == "Scenarios"] <- "Scenarios or designs"

The quantities with exact counterparts in the package (expected numbers of events and dropouts by group at calendar times, state occupation probabilities, survival functions, bounds, the per-patient covariances of the statistics, the quantities of PWEALL, lrstat, rpact and gsDesign, the values printed in their vignettes, and the expected values and probabilities of stopping of the simulations) are judged. The criteria are 4se (within 4 Monte Carlo standard errors), 4se_p (within 4 standard errors computed from the package value), and abs:x or rel:x (absolute or relative difference at most x):

judged <- vd[vd$judgement != "INFO", ]
crit <- as.data.frame(table(criterion = judged$criterion, judgement = judged$judgement))
knitr::kable(crit[crit$Freq > 0, ], row.names = FALSE)

In total 1,726 values pass, 3 are explained and 0 fail.

The mean, standard deviation and correlation of the log-rank statistics, the power and the type I error are asymptotic approximations and are recorded as INFO with the difference in units of the standard error:

info <- vd[vd$judgement == "INFO" & is.finite(vd$se_used) & vd$se_used > 0, ]
z <- info$diff / info$se_used
hist(z, breaks = 40, main = "", xlab = "(simulation - package) / standard error")

Of the 2,102 INFO rows with a standard error, 1,679 are within 2 standard errors and 86 differ by more than 4. These rows, by quantity and by the approximation compared (column variant), and the ten largest differences:

big <- info[abs(z) > 4, ]
big$variant[big$variant == ""] <- "(none)"
table(quantity = big$quantity)

The standard deviation of the statistic with variance = "alternative" does not include the variability of the estimated variance (see vignette("group-sequential")), and the Schoenfeld approximation of the mean (mean = "schoenfeld") is less accurate when the hazard ratio changes over time, as in V2 (see the introductory article, vignette("DesignComplexSurvival")). The numbers of enrolled patients at the first look of the simulated design E1 (source python_expected) differ for the reason given in the next section.

Expected values and conditional power

Under the design scenario, variance = "null" takes the correlations of the statistics from the information, whereas rpact and gsDesign take them from the event fractions. The stopping probabilities of the package are therefore compared with rpact and gsDesign::gsProbability() with tolerances above the differences that this causes, and the probabilities recomputed from the bounds and means of the package with the correlations of the event fractions are compared at 1e-6, which checks the definitions. The conditional powers under the design scenario are INFO rows, and those under the null hypothesis, the current trend and a hazard ratio, which use the correlations of the events, are compared with gsCP() at 1e-5. The values printed in the rpact vignette are recomputed with the correlations of the event fractions, as rpact computes them, and the conditional powers printed in the gsDesign vignette with the futility bounds of gsDesign. The explained values are the expected numbers of enrolled patients of the simulated design E1, whose first analysis is expected close to the end of accrual, so that the variability of its time lowers the simulated mean number of enrolled patients, which the package ignores, and the futility bound by beta spending of the gsDesign vignette at the second analysis, which gsDesign computes with the correlations of the event fractions. The designs and tolerances are listed in the README.md of inst/validation/.

Type I error with unequal allocation

In the simulations, the rejection rate under the null hypothesis of the design with 2:1 allocation and looks at 75 and 150 deaths was above the nominal level. Larger simulations showed that this comes from the skewness of the log-rank statistic with unequal allocation and few events (see the last section of vignette("group-sequential")).

Rerunning the checks

FastSurvival and PWEALL are needed only to rerun inst/validation/, which also uses lrstat (0.3.4 or later), rpact and gsDesign. The README.md of each folder describes how to run the scripts, the criteria and the files. Every compared value is listed with its judgment in results/summary.csv, and results/summary.md summarizes the results.

References

Danzer MF, Rufibach K, Beyersmann J, Schmidt R (2025). Exhausting the type I error level in event-driven group-sequential designs with a closed testing procedure for progression-free and overall survival. arXiv:2512.08658.

Kim K, Tsiatis AA (1990). Study duration for clinical trials with survival response and early stopping rule. Biometrics 46:81-92.

Ortega-Villa AM, Grieco MC, Rubenstein K, Wang J, Proschan MA (2025). Futility monitoring in clinical trials. Statistics in Medicine 44:e70157.
